pr_title: portable: add 'reattach' verb and DBUS interface
pr_body:
Add 'upgrade' verb to portablectl, and corresponding DBUS interface
to systemd-portabled.
Takes the same parameters as 'attach', but it will do a 'detach' (and
it will refuse to proceed if it cannot be done) first, matching on
the unversioned prefix of the new image. Eg:

portablectl upgrade /tmp/foo_2.raw

will cause foo_1.raw to be detached.

The key difference with a manual 'detach old' plus 'attach new' is that
the running units are not disturbed until after the attach completed,
and if --now is passed they are then restarted.
A 'detach' is not allowed normally if the units are running.

By using a restart-after-deploy method, 'upgrade' allows for minimal
interruption of service and also for features that only work on restart
(eg: file descriptor store) to work as intended.

Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/13621
pr_comments: hmm, not sure i grok this. what happens if the unit files in the image change, or one is added or removed?

> hmm, not sure i grok this. what happens if the unit files in the image change, or one is added or removed?

If it changes or something is added, then it all works as expected: daemon-reload after the UpgradeImage returns, and a Restart is called on all the units listed as "changes" in the return value of the dbus method, just like on Attach.

I did forget to handle the case when a unit is removed though (d'oh) as it's not my typical use case - the return list can be used to handle that as well, I'll fix it tomorrow so that units that disappear are stopped instead.
btw, why call this "upgrade"? why not just "reattach"? i.e. is there anything that implies upwards ordering of the version?
hmm, and what about enabling units when oyu do an upgrade like that? restarting is one thing, but there might be new units to enable

> btw, why call this "upgrade"? why not just "reattach"? i.e. is there anything that implies upwards ordering of the version?

No particular reason - I mean my use case is having fast servicing when I need to upgrade the image (CVE fixes or whatever), so that's where it came from. I'll change it to reattach.

> hmm, and what about enabling units when oyu do an upgrade like that? restarting is one thing, but there might be new units to enable

Good point, will fix that as well tomorrow.
Renamed the verb/interface from 'upgrade' to 'reattach' as requested, and also now handling the case where units are removed or are new and need to be enabled. PTAL!
Updated again. Also moved the mksquashfs outside of the test script - as the mksquashfs command segfaults on the ubuntu CI (!!?)

issue_context.title: RFE: portablectl update
issue_context.body: Implement `portablectl update` to update the contents of an attached portable service from a new image.
comments: In the meantime, is there a recommended way to update portable services ? Should I detach the image, update it, and re-attach it ? Can I do this with minimal downtime ?

in theory you don't even need to detach, 
 * update the units
 * reload systemd
and you're done.
Opened https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/18440 to add an "upgrade" verb, that allows changing the image, even with a new version suffix, with minimal downtime and preserving FD store and so on.

review_comments: is this really so? i mean, if the unit files changed we might want to restart the unit too, no?
Yes - that's the second list in the return values signature. You need to be able to tell which is which, so they are separated.

From the commit message:

> The DBUS interface returns two lists: first the removals from the detach
that were not immediately re-added in the attach, so that the caller
can stop the relevant units, and then the list of additions that are
either new or updates, so that the caller can restart/enable the
relevant units. portablectl already implements this with the existing
--now/--enable switches.
